task: Run the W2-50 (DAEO-kl5e) ticket loop up to the CIT-P: the test designer, my red check, a product-spec worker for `docs/changes/W2-50-CIT-P.md`, a lead checkpoint, then return the CIT-P to the owner as a package (Q-15).

status: PACKAGES. The tests are committed and fail for the reasons their README gives. The CIT-P is fully drafted but not committed: the guard refused the product-spec worker's write. It now goes to the owner (Q-15) with four smaller questions. The engineer has not started.

work_completed:
- Identity checked: `orchestrator`, `DAEO-kl5e`, `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-50`, branch `w2/W2-50`. I started fresh (there was no lead checkpoint).
- Read the governing material: the w2 prompt sections 4–6, 9, 10, 12, 13 and Appendix A; WBS sections 0, 2 (W2-50), 5 and 6; the ticket; W2-M355; DEC-728, 723, 159, 096, 135, 136, 413, 462, 476, 498 and 731–733; CAP-33; the brief templates.
- Test designer (`td-1`): started in the launch form with no denial. It committed 139 cases in `tests/acceptance/W2-50/`.
- My red check, run to the end: 48 failed, 91 passed. Each failure is red for the reason the README states:
  - the guard refuses the session's own folder;
  - `allowWrite` holds only the temp folder;
  - the launcher creates no folder;
  - `rmdir` of the root is allowed;
  - the secrets check follows a link from `.gov-runtime/` into the root.
  The 91 that pass are refusals the guard already makes; they must still hold after the change.
- Product-spec worker (`ps-citp-1`): started with no denial. Its single write to `docs/changes/W2-50-CIT-P.md` was refused by the guard (it did not retry). It left the complete 318-line CIT-P as a draft. I reviewed the draft and kept a copy at `.gov-runtime/scratch/lead/W2-50-CIT-P.draft.md` (sha256 `776d1338…10a5`).
- Wrote `.gov-runtime/scratch/lead/CHECKPOINT.md` and the record `CP-DAEO-kl5e-0004` (`--next "CIT-P with the owner (Q-15); engineer after approval"`), and committed the record.

evidence:
- `74403441`, trailers: `Task: DAEO-kl5e`, `Role: independent-test-designer`, `Implements: DEC-728`, `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5`.
- `04e7a9eb`, trailers: `Task: DAEO-kl5e`, `Implements: DEC-728`, `Role: orchestrator`, `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5`.
- Branch head `04e7a9eb`; tree clean. No commit appeared that nobody in this ticket made.
- `PYTHONPATH=/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-50/src python3 -c "import gov; print(gov.__file__)"` printed `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-50/src/gov/__init__.py`.
- The main repository's `.git/hooks` held no `pre-commit` before each commit.
- `test -e ~/gov-os-runs` prints ABSENT, before and after.
- The guard's refusal, verbatim: "PreToolUse:Write hook error: Write to '/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-50/docs/changes/W2-50-CIT-P.md' denied for role 'product-spec'". The cause: in `src/gov/guard/decide.py` (`_get_allowed_paths`), a session gets no paths unless its role equals the ticket's `role:`, which is `engineer`.
- Logs: `.gov-runtime/scratch/lead/log/td-1.json`, `ps-citp-1.json`, `red-1.txt` (`red-1.exit` = 1).

tests:
- `tests/acceptance/W2-50` (red check, `PYTHONPATH` set to this worktree): 48 failed, 91 passed, 169 s.
  - 31 are guard cases for the own folder.
  - 14 are launcher cases (the sandbox write list, the folder existing when the session starts, survival).
  - 2 are links followed by the secrets check, and 1 is `rmdir` of the root.
- Product-spec worker: W1-30 r15, W1-27 doctor r5, W1-11 and W1-26 taxonomy gave 175 passed. The CIT-P file was not in the tree for that run.
- `validate_s1.py` crashes at line 67 with `KeyError: 'wbs_id'`. This was there before this ticket (P-E).
- No other suites were run; there was no implementation to verify.

discoveries:
- A product-spec worker cannot write on this ticket, because its `role:` is engineer. The CIT-E will hit the same refusal (P-B).
- The secrets check follows links on purpose (`os.walk(..., followlinks=True)` in `src/gov/secrets/__init__.py`) and has no exclusion option. That file is outside `allowed_paths`. W1-15's B4 test requires it to keep following a linked store folder elsewhere, so any exclusion must name `~/gov-os-runs` only (P-C).
- The guard does not judge `git clone` destinations. A session without a sandbox (orchestrator, lead) could clone into another ticket's folder or into `~/gov-os-workbench`. This predates the ticket (P-D).
- The guard does not judge `rmdir` today (reading R7).
- DEC-313 refuses `--add-dir`. Claude Code's own permission layer may therefore keep a launched session's Write and Edit tools out of `~/gov-os-runs`, leaving Bash only (CIT-P §6.3).
- Nothing says whether the guard's seventh role, `ticket-lead`, counts as "any role" (§6.5). Whether a closed ticket's folder can still be written has no source (§6.4).
- CAP-58.d's text will name neither exception: the temp folder and the session's own folder (§6.6).
- I reproduced the `validate_s1.py` crash at this ticket's base. It has been there since `4190c39e`: DAEO-rd0g and DAEO-swdu have no `wbs_id` (DEC-730 item 3).

risks:
- The CIT-P exists only as a gitignored draft in this worktree until P-B is answered. If the worktree is removed, it is lost (there are two copies, both in this worktree).
- R2 (the launcher creates the folder) and R7 (judging `rmdir`) reach slightly past the ticket's "the list only" and "the outside-repository rule only" wording. The CIT-P names both.

lessons:
- On a ticket whose `role:` is engineer, product-spec writes are refused. Briefs for this ticket's docs need the role settled first.
- Tests that use a temporary `HOME` must keep it apart from `TMPDIR`. The suite does this; otherwise the guard's temp-folder allowance hides the refusals.

proposed_decisions:
- **P-A (Q-15, owner; CAP-33): approve the W2-50 CIT-P.** The draft is at `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-50/.gov-runtime/scratch/lead/W2-50-CIT-P.draft.md`.
  - Question: apply now, defer or re-baseline (DEC-105). Approving it also approves readings R1–R8 (§5): R1 and R3 (high), R2 (medium), R4 (medium), R5 (medium, see P-C), R6 (high), R7 (high), R8 (medium).
  - Why now: the engineer may not start without it. W2-14, W2-15a/b, W2-24 and W2-27 wait on W2-50, and there are about 5 days of slack.
  - What it loosens: only `~/gov-os-runs/<own ticket>/`, in the guard and in the sandbox write list.
  - What stays refused (each held by tests): another ticket's folder; the root itself; escapes by `..`, symbolic link or hard link; no or forged ticket; anywhere else outside the repository; the workbench and other worktrees.
  - Reversibility: a code revert. Folders already made stay on disk.
  - Cost: about 120 LOC.
  - Recommendation: apply now, with R1–R8 as read. Confidence: high on the change, medium on R2, R4, R5 and R8.
- **P-B (orchestrator or owner): where the CIT-P and CIT-E get committed.** The guard refuses product-spec on this engineer-role ticket, and I write nothing under `docs/` except probe records.
  - Options:
    - (a) after approval, the engineer (the ticket's role) commits the CIT-P draft word for word, with the owner's answers, in a commit of its own before any code, and later writes the CIT-E;
    - (b) a decision lets the lead commit both records, like DEC-733 does for probe records;
    - (c) change the ticket's role or the guard rule, which widens the guard and is the owner's call.
  - Reversibility: (a) and (b) are reversible.
  - Recommendation: (a). Confidence: medium.
- **P-C (owner): the path for the secrets-indexing exclusion** (CIT-P §6.1). R5 cannot be built inside the listed paths.
  - Options:
    - (i) add `src/gov/secrets/__init__.py` (the link rule only) to `allowed_paths`;
    - (ii) point the check's command at an entry in the new module;
    - (iii) keep following links, which is stricter on secrets; the test designer rewrites the two link cases and "never scans it" gets a narrower reading.
  - Recommendation: (i), the smallest and most explicit, with W1-15 B4 kept green. Confidence: medium.
- **P-D (owner, finish-line rule): `git clone` destinations are not judged by the guard.** This is a fail-open for sessions without a sandbox, and it predates this ticket.
  - Options: judge them in W2-50 (more scope and more tests), or add a Wave 2 row triaged to W2-09, which edits `decide.py` next.
  - Recommendation: a row for W2-09. Confidence: medium.
- **P-E (orchestrator): `validate_s1.py` crashes at line 67 (`KeyError: 'wbs_id'`) on DAEO-rd0g and DAEO-swdu.** It blocks every lead's "ALL PASS" check. Recommendation: make the validator fall back to `external-ref`, or apply DEC-730 item 3 early, outside this ticket. Confidence: medium.

unresolved:
- P-A to P-E.
- CIT-P §6.3 (the file tools in a launched session: a residual or an experiment), §6.4 (a closed ticket's folder), §6.5 (`ticket-lead` as "any role"), §6.6 (CAP-58 text, a Wave 2 list row).
- Learning metrics so far: no KPI disputes, no tests rewritten, no implementation iterations.

recommended_next_action: Put P-A (with the CIT-P draft) and P-C/P-D to the owner as Q-15, decide P-B and P-E, then send a fresh lead to resume from `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-50/.gov-runtime/scratch/lead/CHECKPOINT.md`.
